NVDA acquiring Groq - For Nvidia, the strategic value is in strengthening the most sensitive parts of its inference stack: token-level TPS during decoding, and effective bandwidth under complex workloads and multi-tenant, fragmented inference traffic. Given Groq’s heavy reliance on SRAM, there has been a heated discussion on its impact on HBM demand which we think is misunderstood.

META Acquiring Manus
Based on our understanding, META is acquiring Manus for approximately \$2.5 billion, at a valuation of roughly 20x ARR, with Manus having reached \$125 million in ARR.
Manus does not face any near-term survival issues. If we consider only its paying users, the company has significantly positive gross margins. When factoring in free users, our latest understanding indicates that gross margins are also approaching breakeven.
Manus possesses exceptionally strong engineering capabilities and has been continuously optimizing agent cost structures through router, cache, and other engineering optimizations. Additionally, the company maintains excellent partnerships with Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenAI, enabling them to purchase APIs at very favorable discounts.
Compared with other agent companies, Manus has always been remarkable for its development speed and iteration efficiency. Its founder, Red, is a serial entrepreneur. Co ‑ founder Peak single ‑ handedly built the Mammoth browser at the age of 18, and co ‑ founder Zhangtao is a veteran product manager who previously served as Head of Product at Light Year, the LLM startup founded by Wang Huiwen.
META currently has two large language models under development. One follows the Llama technical path, though the team has lowered expectations - the model originally benchmarked against Gemini 3.0 is now more appropriately targeting Gemini 2.5 based on current progress. Their future flagship model, Avocado, may launch in Q2 2026, aiming to surpass Gemini 3.0.

We believe META’s acquisition of Manus offers significant value
Currently, META AI uses Gemini extensively alongside Llama. Acquiring Manus will significantly improve META AI’s user experience while increasing Llama’s usage share.
META AI has substantial value for advertising revenue, as it can help META generate more sales leads. For instance, automotive and financial insurance clients have historically advertised primarily on Google due to lack of sales leads on META. As META AI’s user experience improves, META stands to capture more sales leads.
Considering META’s track record of imposing clear earn-out requirements on founding teams during acquisitions like Scale.AI - for example, requiring Alexander Wong to complete Avocado training within a specified timeframe when acquiring Scale.AI - we believe META has also set explicit earn-out targets for Red Xiao and the two other co-founders, likely related to META AI and agent commercialization.
DeepSeek Releases New mHC Paper
DeepSeek has released a new paper on mHC.
Although there has already been a lot of discussion in the market about mHC, we believe the core changes haven’t really been addressed.
mHC is primarily aimed at solving the instability issues in large-scale model pretraining.
Over the past 1–2 years, frontier LLM labs such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini have invested heavily in tackling pretraining instability so they can pretrain larger models; Gemini 3 and GPT ‑ 5.2 are the most representative examples of this trend.
With mHC, DeepSeek is now able to train models using much larger compute at scale. The techniques introduced in this paper do not change the fundamental technical roadmap of frontier models.
TPU volume update
On New Year’s Eve, there was rumour circulating around TPU volume cut. Our channel check suggests there has never been any talk of cutting TPU demand from 4mn to 3mn in 2026. AVGO wanted to increase from 240k CoWoS to 270k CoWoS in

October, but due to TSMC’s capacity bottleneck, this additional order request hasn’t been approved yet. Similarly, NVDA’s request to increase from 600k CoWoS to 800k CoWoS has only been fulfilled to 700k so far.
We already released the latest TPU Capacity tracking report two weeks ago. According to our Taiwan supply chain monitoring, the actual capacity TPU can secure is around 3.3-3.4mn. In addition to AVGO’s 3mn capacity, MTK also has 0.3- 0.4mn. The Asian market, based on continuously increasing optical module orders, has extrapolated TPU capacity to exceed 4mn. This is because they only considered the demand for optical modules in scale-up 3D torus networks, without accounting for the significant increase in DCN demand. We’ll soon release a report discussing DCN. So despite TSMC’s very tight capacity, optical modules corresponding to TPU are still seeing continuous order increases. As TPU capacity increases substantially in 2027, the sustainability of optical modules will be further validated. As for LITE, GOOG has always hoped LITE could account for 20% of next year’s optical module demand, depending on actual supply.
SNOW Acquiring Observe
This is a very interesting deal. We’ve been following this company since many years ago. Observe is a Snowflake Native company - its Data Layer has been Native based on Snowflake for a long time. In 2023 or sometime around then, Observe posted a tweet mentioning that they contributed 40mn Snowflake queries per day, accounting for 2% of Snowflake’s query volume at one point. Later, with the rapid growth of Snowpark, more lower-priced queries emerged, diluting Observe’s share of Snowflake queries.
Actually, there was another Snowflake Native startup growing even faster at the time - Lacework, also incubated by Sutter Hill - but it quickly ran into difficulties. I didn’t expect that after 2-3 years, we’d be discussing cases like Observe again.
Log data doesn’t necessarily have to be stored in log products - it’s essentially a combination of structured/semi-structured data, so it can exist in Snowflake and Databricks in structured/semi-structured form. If customers ultimately want an integrated data platform that can manage all their various data types, hoping to complete the data processing needed for data applications by reducing data copies and ETL, then naturally they can choose Snowflake and Databricks along with their Monitor, Log, and SIEM products on top.

Moreover, platforms like Snowflake/Databricks with separated storage and compute have good economics - for the same cost, data can be retained for longer periods, which has significant benefits for monitoring and tracing back security issues. Compared to other Monitor, Log, and SIEM vendors, these Snowflake native vendors can focus all their efforts on the application layer - they don’t need to modify ESTC anymore, so they can leave the compute and storage optimization work to Snowflake.
